inspiration: Launcher look: a wide painted vista (about 2.2:1) sits behind dark translucent glass panels with a thin gold rule and rounded corners, and the painting is shown at a pixelated scale. Keep the calm, painted backdrop and the quiet panels. Ref: dereth/launcher/README.md lines 174 to 181.

Two-register UI: chunky pixel-grid frames for buttons and the main action plate, set against plain serif type for headings and body text. The contrast makes controls read as game and text read as text. Ref: dereth/launcher/README.md line 176.

Window frame kit packed at integer scales: named corner, edge and fill pieces are authored once and packed at 1x, 2x and 3x so frames stay crisp. Ref: dereth/client/crates/horizon/pieces/manifest.json (entries such as window.tl and window.top).

Slot icons on one flat ground: 32 x 32 pictures sit on a single dark ground so any transparent pixel reads as the empty slot. A small manifest tells the packer which picture goes where. Ref: core/client-runtime/assets/classic-portal/pack.tsv and cloak.png.

Lit and unlit pairs: a small book-style icon comes in a normal and a lit version (journal.png and journal-lit.png) for a state change. Simple, cheap, readable at small size. Ref: core/client-runtime/assets/classic-portal/journal-lit.png.

Three-hue sigil set: three 32 x 32 charms in different hues (red, blue, yellow) mark distinct categories at a glance. Ref: core/client-runtime/assets/classic-portal/sigil-red.png, sigil-blue.png, sigil-yellow.png.

Nameplate colour key in the Horizon HUD: people, fightable creatures and players get three hues, so the nearby crowd reads at a glance. Ref: dereth/client/crates/horizon/README.md, table 'How the game's concepts are drawn'.

briefs.label: Three-hue sigil charm set
briefs.why: A 32 px badge in three hues tells categories apart at a glance, and a lit and unlit pair shows state with no extra art.
briefs.keep: Small 32 px badge silhouettes; one hue per category; a lit and unlit pair for each.
briefs.change: Our own emblem shape (not a plain round badge); our own palette; our own glyph inside.

briefs.label: Wide painted vista behind glass panels
briefs.why: A wide, calm painting lets the panels and buttons sit over open space instead of over a busy scene.
briefs.keep: Wide letterbox painting; dark translucent panels with a thin gold rule; pixelated scaling.
briefs.change: Our own subject with one dominant landmark; our own palette; no locale or creature names in the file names.
briefs.ref: dereth/launcher/assets/background/wilderness.png (file present, not viewed; class C, inspiration only)

briefs.label: Three-scale window frame kit
briefs.why: Corners and edges reused everywhere give one consistent frame family that stays crisp at each scale.
briefs.keep: Corner, edge and fill pieces; integer scales 1x, 2x, 3x; a named manifest.
briefs.change: Our own bevel and corner radius; a different corner ornament; our own palette.

briefs.label: Three-hue nameplate key
briefs.why: Friend, foe and player colours read at a glance in a crowded scene.
briefs.keep: Three hues mapped to three roles; a clear key in the HUD.
briefs.change: Hues away from the green, yellow and blue trio; add a shape cue so the key works for colour-blind players.
briefs.ref: dereth/client/crates/horizon/README.md (table 'How the game's concepts are drawn')
